- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in second half of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment environments; apply +1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment > 0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillation, model exhibits lag; add 0.2–0.5% lag correction to early periods.
